title: The Blind Man and the Cripple

keywords: the blind man and the cripple
full_text:
In a town at the edge of a great forest lived two men afflicted with misfortune: one was strong of limb and fleet of foot, but completely blind from birth; the other possessed sharp, piercing eyesight and keen intellect, but his legs were withered, and he could not walk a single pace without crutches.

One afternoon, a fierce wildfire swept down from the dry pine hills toward the town. The church bells rang in panic, and the citizens fled in all directions across the river.

The blind man stumbled in terror against walls and trees, unable to find the road to safety; the crippled man sat upon his porch, weeping as he watched the flames advance, unable to carry his body across the fields.

As the smoke grew thick, the crippled man shouted through the haze: 'Ho, strong brother! Come toward the sound of my voice!'

The blind man felt his way to the porch. The crippled man proposed a noble partnership: 'You have sturdy legs to walk, and I have sharp eyes to see! Lift me upon your broad shoulders: I shall be your eyes to guide your steps, and you shall be my feet to carry us through the smoke!'

The blind man lifted the cripple onto his back.

With the cripple directing every turn—'Turn right at the well! Step over the ditch! Straight down the willow path!'—the blind man strode swiftly through the burning smoke, avoiding deep crevices and burning branches, until they crossed the river safely onto the green, unburned meadows!

The surviving citizens cheered their miraculous escape. The two men formed a lifelong partnership, establishing an orchard and living in honored fellowship, proving that our limitations are transformed into triumph when we combine our strengths in cooperative love.
moral: When diverse talents unite in selfless cooperation, no obstacle is insurmountable.
